questions.q: Input window = [10, 12, 14, 16]. Block 1 backcast = [10, 12, 14, 16]. What is the residual passed to block 2?
Block forecasts are [18, 20] and [1, −1]. What is the final forecast?
why: Correct: the forecasts are added: 18 + 1 = 19 and 20 − 1 = 19.

questions.q: Which statement about N-BEATS is true?
options: It uses fully connected layers with no recurrence and no attention.
It needs a separate model for each horizon step only.
why: No, one block outputs the whole forecast vector.

questions.q: What does N-HiTS change compared with N-BEATS?
options: Multi-rate input pooling and hierarchical interpolation of outputs.

questions.q: You must explain to a manager how much of a forecast comes from trend and how much from season. Which setup helps?
options: Interpretable N-BEATS with trend and seasonal blocks.
why: Correct: you can plot each block's forecast piece.
Generic blocks have no fixed meaning.

questions.q: Your N-BEATS model is worse than seasonal naive on the test set. First thing to check?
options: Window length covers a full season, scaling uses train data only, and the split is by time.
why: Correct: these are the most common problems.
More layers rarely fix a setup issue.
